:::{#exm-continuous-on-sqrt}
#### Continuity on $\lbrack 0, 1\rbrack$ uses one-sided limits at the endpoints

Let $f(x) = \sqrt{x}$, the [square root](algebra.qmd#def-square-root), defined for $x \ge 0$.
Because $f$ is undefined for $x < 0$,
only the right-hand limit of $f$ at $0$ makes sense,
and @def-continuous-on-interval asks only for that [one-sided limit](calculus-derivatives.qmd#def-one-sided-limit) at the endpoint $0$.
Here $f$ is continuous at every point of $(0, 1)$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lim_{x \to 0^+} \sqrt{x} &= 0 \\
&= f(0),
\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lim_{x \to 1^-} \sqrt{x} &= 1 \\
&= f(1),
\end{aligned}
$$

so $f$ is [continuous on](#def-continuous-on-interval) $[0, 1]$.
@fig-continuous-on-sqrt shows its [graph](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-graph), which has no break anywhere on $[0, 1]$.

:::{#fig-continuous-on-sqrt}

```{r}
#| label: continuous-on-sqrt-plot
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   The graph of the square root of x for x from 0 to 1: an unbroken
#|   curve rising steeply from the point (0, 0) and flattening as it
#|   reaches the point (1, 1). Both endpoints are marked with filled dots.
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 4.5
x_values <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 401)
root_values <- sqrt(x_values)
curve <- tibble::tibble(x = x_values, y = root_values)
endpoints <- tibble::tribble(
  ~x, ~y,
  0, 0,
  1, 1
)

curve |>
  ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y) +
  ggplot2::geom_line() +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = endpoints, size = 2.5)
```

The [square root](algebra.qmd#def-square-root) $f(x) = \sqrt{x}$ on $[0, 1]$.
The curve meets both filled [endpoints](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/sets.html#def-interval), $(0, 0)$ and $(1, 1)$, without a jump.
:::
